title: Desert dust scoured by natural winds could save New Mexico solar operators thousands in O&M costs
content: While utility-scale solar asset managers across the southwestern United States frequently battle the costly power-degrading impacts of atmospheric "soiling," a breakthrough study reveals that operators downwind of the world’s largest gypsum dunefield may have an unexpected financial ally: the desert wind itself.

title: Arizona appeals court vacates APS solar-specific charge over due process violations
content: The Arizona Court of Appeals has struck down a controversial solar-specific grid charge imposed by Arizona Public Service (APS), ruling that regulators pushed the fee through without proper public notice or fair hearings. While the three-judge panel vacated the charge based strictly on procedural due process violations, it stopped short of ruling on the legality of the fee itself—leaving the door open for future regulatory battles.
